decisions.reason: SOL clarifies that the corpses’ eyes are wide open without changing the image.
SOL keeps the sense of thousands approaching while avoiding BASE’s added target, “on them.”
“Deep despair” preserves the contrast and intensity of the omen.
“Jamukha Khan” naturally conveys the Korean title and name.
SOL preserves the arrival and reinforcements, including the source’s rhetorical emphasis.
SOL keeps the morale reversal and the defenders’ returning fatigue and fear.
SOL conveys the blood as proof of the commander’s fierce fighting in cleaner prose.
“Given the battle everything he had” keeps the sense that he fought with all his strength.
SOL drops the flawless orders and the source’s water-tight image.
“Against” keeps the sense of fighting the enemies without changing the losses.
The future-in-context phrasing preserves the image of the pebbles breaking first.
SOL keeps the tangled battle, his rooted stance, and the retainer’s words being drowned out.
SOL turns the fragment into a natural sentence without changing the tug.
SOL makes clear that the desperate face belongs to the retainer.
SOL replaces the specific retainer with the generic “man,” dropping his role.
SOL omits the source’s concluding point that withdrawal is the best strategy.
“Tightened his grip” naturally conveys his firming hold on the hilt.
The Keshik was approaching and trying to get through the guards; SOL changes this to having already broken through.
SOL drops the source’s indication that the retainer followed him again.
“Leaving everything that follows to her” preserves the sense of entrusting the aftermath to Seowol.
“Defeated commander” preserves the defeated leader’s meaning without changing the scene.
SOL joins the promise and its content naturally without changing what he vowed.
The plural “crowns” fits the defenders’ heads and keeps the shiver’s path.
SOL drops the source’s quality of vague, undefined helplessness.
SOL changes inward muttering into asking himself a question, losing the source’s action.
SOL removes BASE’s unsupported “silver” metaphor while keeping the rebuke.
“Clumsy at it” naturally clarifies that Jamukha means Mukyung’s attempt to provoke him.
SOL drops the source’s momentary timing cue before Mukyung laughs.
The source asks whether he is to surrender to Jamukha; SOL’s “Me, of all people?” changes the object.
“The tops of his feet” accurately renders the specific image of licking the insteps.
“Across its white blade” naturally preserves the image of speaking beyond the raised sword.
“Spare your life” makes explicit the source’s promise to let him live; SOL’s phrasing is less clear.
The source says putting on a leash is insufficient; SOL substitutes a collar.
SOL changes being restrained by a sturdy leash into merely being kept in a collar.
The source explicitly rejects the fear interpretation as wrong; “No” softens that correction.
SOL stamps “hyung” onto narration where BASE naturally renders the ordinary reference as “older brother.”
SOL loses the source’s image of his gaze sinking deeply.
SOL drops the physical gesture of parting his lips before speaking.
The tense shift preserves the smile’s fading as Mukyung steps forward.
SOL omits the source’s “single phrase” beat before the insult.
SOL conveys dozens of horns sounding at once in natural English.
“Hadn’t come from the nomads alone” keeps the source’s revelation in natural English.
